title: Chasing Under Pressure: Does Kolkata Knight Riders Bat Differently When the Target Climbs?
dek: Does Kolkata Knight Riders' batting change as the target climbs? Chasing records by target band and by the required rate at halfway show where pressure bites.
excerpt: Kolkata Knight Riders have won more of their chases than the league average. The data shows how quickly a chase slips away as the target rises past two hundred.
author: CricField Editorial Desk
keyTakeaways: KKR have won {{ev:chase-t}} of their chases; the league figure is {{ev:chase-l}}.
IPL sides chasing under 150 won {{ev:chase-lunder}}; chasing 200 or more, {{ev:chase-l200}}.
KKR have won {{ev:chase-t200}} of their {{ev:chase-t200n}} chases of 200 or more.

sections.heading: The Target Sets the Tone
body: Chasing in T20 is a different sport at different totals. Across every IPL chase with a result, sides set under 150 won {{ev:chase-lunder}} of the time; set 200 or more, {{ev:chase-l200}}.
Kolkata Knight Riders have won {{ev:chase-t}} of their chases overall against a league figure of {{ev:chase-l}}.

sections.heading: Pressure at Halfway
body: The required run rate after ten overs is a sharper measure of pressure than the target itself. Across the league, sides needing nine to eleven an over at halfway won {{ev:chase-rr-911}} of the time; sides needing eleven to thirteen won {{ev:chase-rr-1113}}.
Against the biggest targets, KKR have won {{ev:chase-t200}} of {{ev:chase-t200n}} chases of 200 or more.

sections.heading: Batting Differently as the Target Climbs
body: A big target changes the batting order's job: the powerplay has to be bigger and the middle overs cannot be used for consolidation. The other lever is wickets in hand, which decide how hard a side can swing in the last five overs.
For KKR, the practical plan is to set halfway checkpoints for each target band and promote hitters when the side is behind them.

sections.heading: Dew, Toss and Venue
body: Chasing records carry conditions with them. Dew in evening matches, the toss and the ground all shift the odds, and none of them are controlled in a simple record by target band.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Chase the Checkpoint, Not the Total
body: Kolkata Knight Riders have been better chasers than the league, and the gap matters most against big targets. The evidence supports chasing to a required-rate checkpoint at halfway rather than to the total.
If the asking rate at ten overs is manageable, protecting wickets keeps the finish available; if it is not, the hitters have to come in early.

methodology: Regulation innings only (super overs excluded). Run rates use all runs per legal ball times six. Every figure is generated from the CricField warehouse by scripts/editorial/engine. Target bands use the first-innings total. Required rate at halfway = runs needed after ten overs divided by overs remaining. Team bands with fewer than eight chases are not shown.
